sentences.en: This episode is brought to you by Sky.
sentences.zh: 本集由 Sky 赞助播出。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, we are talking about dragons today, and I know that you are as excited as I am about the return of House of the Dragon,
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，我们今天来聊聊龙。我知道你和我一样，对《龙之家族》的回归感到非常兴奋，

sentences.en: because actually it's been two years, almost two years, since we last saw Matt Smith, Emma Darcy, Olivia Cooke on House of the Dragon,
sentences.zh: 因为距离我们上次在《龙之家族》中看到马特·史密斯、艾玛·达西和奥利维亚·库克，已经过去两年了，几乎整整两年，

sentences.en: and now they are returning for the biggest TV event of the summer.
sentences.zh: 而现在，他们将回归，带来这个夏天最盛大的电视盛事。

sentences.en: So, more characters and, best of all, five new dragons.
sentences.zh: 所以，会有更多角色，最棒的是，还有五条新龙。

sentences.en: So, Tom, you'll remember the big hullabaloo about King Aegon II's coronation, and you'll remember what happened to his cousin, Lucerys Targaryen, murdered by a dragon.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你还记得关于伊耿二世国王加冕礼的那场大骚动吧，你也记得他的堂弟路斯里斯·瓦列利安遭遇了什么——被龙杀害了。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我记得。

sentences.en: So, season two will see the much-anticipated civil war between the Greens and the Blacks unfold, as, Tom, the dance of the dragons truly begins.
sentences.zh: 所以，第二季将展现备受期待的“黑党”与“绿党”之间的内战，汤姆，因为“血龙狂舞”真正开始了。

sentences.en: The realm is divided.
sentences.zh: 王国分裂了。

sentences.en: All of Westeros must choose a side.
sentences.zh: 整个维斯特洛都必须选边站。

sentences.en: So, please tune in every Monday.
sentences.zh: 所以，请每周一准时收看。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, there are so many questions.
sentences.zh: 而且，多米尼克，还有太多的疑问了。

sentences.en: Who will win the war?
sentences.zh: 谁会赢得这场战争？

sentences.en: Will Team Black or Team Green claim the Iron Throne?
sentences.zh: 是黑党还是绿党会夺得铁王座？

sentences.en: Which of these factions will triumph in the Dance of the Dragons?
sentences.zh: 在这场“血龙狂舞”中，哪一方会最终获胜？

sentences.en: House of the Dragon is available now exclusively on Sky, and you can, of course, go to sky.com to find out more.
sentences.zh: 《龙之家族》现已在 Sky 独家上线，当然，你可以访问 sky.com 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: A dragon is no idle fancy.
sentences.zh: 龙并非虚妄的幻想。

sentences.en: Whatever may be his origins, in fact or invention, the dragon in legend is a potent creation of men's imagination, richer in significance than his barrow is in gold.
sentences.zh: 无论其起源为何，是事实还是虚构，传说中的龙都是人类想象力的强大产物，其意义远比它坟冢里的黄金更为丰富。

sentences.en: Even today, despite the critics, you may find men not ignorant of tragic legend and history, who have heard of heroes and, indeed, seen them,
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，尽管有批评家，你仍能发现一些人，他们并不无知于悲剧传说和历史，他们听说过英雄，甚至亲眼见过英雄，

sentences.en: who have yet been caught by the fascination of the worm.
sentences.zh: 却依然被这种“长虫”的魅力所俘获。

sentences.en: That was, of course, J.R.R.
sentences.zh: 那当然是 J.R.R.

sentences.en: Tolkien in his great essay,
sentences.zh: 托尔金在他那篇伟大的论文中提到的，

sentences.en: Beowulf, the Monsters and the Critics, which he published in 1936.
sentences.zh: 《贝奥武夫：怪兽与批评家》，发表于 1936 年。

sentences.en: And, Tom, that was an essay that changed the way people thought about
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那篇论文改变了人们对……的看法，

sentences.en: Anglo-Saxon literature, about fantasy literature more generally, I suppose, but also about dragons.
sentences.zh: 我想是对盎格鲁-撒克逊文学，对奇幻文学，当然也对龙的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So he talks about people who've been caught by the fascination of the worm.
sentences.zh: 所以他谈到了那些被“长虫”魅力所俘获的人。

sentences.en: He does, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think pretty clearly there he's talking about himself.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为很明显，他在那里谈论的是他自己。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's obviously a man who is obsessed by dragons.
sentences.zh: 他显然是一个对龙着迷的人。

sentences.en: But since Tolkien wrote that essay, dragons have gone completely mainstream, in part, at least thanks to Tolkien himself.
sentences.zh: 但自从托尔金写下那篇论文后，龙已经完全进入了主流视野，至少部分归功于托尔金本人。

sentences.en: Partly thanks to Tolkien, yeah.
sentences.zh: 部分归功于托尔金，是的。

sentences.en: But more recently, due to the global phenomenon that is Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.
sentences.zh: 但更近一点说，是因为《权力的游戏》和《龙之家族》这一全球现象。

sentences.en: So the novels first by George R.R.
sentences.zh: 首先是乔治·R.R.

sentences.en: Martin, and then the TV series.
sentences.zh: 马丁的小说，然后是电视剧。

sentences.en: So people were very excited, weren't they, when Game of Thrones first came out.
sentences.zh: 所以人们在《权力的游戏》刚出来的时候非常兴奋，不是吗？

sentences.en: I remember watching it, what is it, 10 years ago or something.
sentences.zh: 我记得我是在看它，大概是 10 年前还是什么时候。

sentences.en: The dragons in Game of Thrones, when they start off, dragons are extinct or they're thought to have vanished, and they're in these eggs.
sentences.zh: 《权力的游戏》里的龙，刚开始的时候，龙已经灭绝了，或者被认为已经消失了，它们就在这些蛋里。

sentences.en: And then they hatch at the end of the first series, and it's very exciting.
sentences.zh: 然后在第一季末尾它们孵化了，这非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And they're quite sweet, aren't they, to begin with?
sentences.zh: 而且它们刚开始的时候很可爱，不是吗？

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Kind of little baby dragons.
sentences.zh: 就像小龙宝宝一样。

sentences.en: They're very kind of Gremlins-esque.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像《小魔怪》里的生物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But actually, Game of Thrones, in TV terms, was groundbreaking
sentences.zh: 但实际上，从电视制作的角度来看，《权力的游戏》是开创性的，

sentences.en: because the CGI used for the dragons was extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 因为用于龙的 CGI 特效非常非凡。

sentences.en: I mean, it was the first time anyone had done anything like this that didn't look a little bit fake.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是第一次有人做出看起来不那么虚假的东西。

sentences.en: And actually, as the series went on, the dragons became more and more important because they sort of played the part of...
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，随着剧集的推进，龙变得越来越重要，因为它们扮演了……的角色。

sentences.en: Well, we were talking about this before we started recording, weren't we?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在录制前就在讨论这个，不是吗？

sentences.en: About whether or not the dragons can be likened to weapons of mass destruction.
sentences.zh: 关于龙是否可以被比作大规模杀伤性武器。

sentences.en: And at the end of Game of Thrones, without giving it away to people who haven't...
sentences.zh: 在《权力的游戏》结尾，为了不给还没看的人剧透……

sentences.en: Well, actually, if you've read the books, you haven't got to the end.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，如果你读过书，你还没看到结尾。

sentences.en: But if you've seen the TV series, the dragon's sort of full potential is exploited in a terrifying way.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看过电视剧，龙的全部潜力以一种可怕的方式被利用了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Unleashed in a kind of apocalyptic manner.
sentences.zh: 以一种末日般的方式被释放出来。

sentences.en: And the reason that we're recording this is that today, going out on Sky is House of the Dragon.
sentences.zh: 我们录制这个的原因是，今天在 Sky 上映的是《龙之家族》。

sentences.en: So Series 1 has already gone out, and now Series 2 is coming out.
sentences.zh: 第一季已经播出了，现在第二季要出来了。

sentences.en: And in that series, which you can see on Sky,
sentences.zh: 在这一季中，你可以在 Sky 上看到，

sentences.en: House of the Dragon is...
sentences.zh: 《龙之家族》是……

sentences.en: Well, do you know what?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道吗？

sentences.en: We're being sponsored by Sky.
sentences.zh: 我们是由 Sky 赞助的。

sentences.en: Let's be upfront.
sentences.zh: 我们坦诚一点。

sentences.en: I hope that they will allow me to say that it is quite like Henry VI Part 1, the Shakespeare play that shows us the opening of The Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们允许我说，它很像莎士比亚的剧作《亨利六世：第一部》，展现了“玫瑰战争”的开端。

sentences.en: So it's like The Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像“玫瑰战争”。

sentences.en: It's very, very Shakespearean.
sentences.zh: 非常有莎士比亚风格。

sentences.en: Kind of rival, noble families quarreling over the crown.
sentences.zh: 就像敌对的贵族家庭为了王冠而争吵。

sentences.en: So it's like Shakespeare, only you don't know what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像莎士比亚的作品，只是你不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: And as the name implies, it has a lot of dragons.
sentences.zh: 正如其名，它有很多龙。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the dragon's in House of the Dragon.
sentences.zh: 所以《龙之家族》里的龙。

sentences.en: It's not like in Game of Thrones, where there's the mother of dragons, and she has three dragons.
sentences.zh: 它不像《权力的游戏》那样，有一个龙之母，她有三条龙。

sentences.en: And that makes her a remarkable figure in the context of this world, Westeros.
sentences.zh: 这使她在维斯特洛这个世界背景下成为一个非凡的人物。

sentences.en: But in House of the Dragon, there's a sort of nuclear proliferation, isn't there, of dragons?
sentences.zh: 但在《龙之家族》中，龙有一种核扩散的趋势，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I think that dragons kind of play the role of tactical nuclear weapons, so battlefield nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 我认为龙扮演了战术核武器的角色，也就是战场核武器。

sentences.en: And we see the origins of the family of Daenerys, the mother of dragons.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了龙之母丹妮莉丝家族的起源。

sentences.en: So it's the Targaryens.
sentences.zh: 所以是坦格利安家族。

sentences.en: They have come from overseas.
sentences.zh: 他们从海外而来。

sentences.en: They've brought their dragons with them, and this has enabled them to conquer the continent of Westeros.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了龙，这使他们能够征服维斯特洛大陆。

sentences.en: And basically, the plot of House of the Dragon is civil war within the Targaryen family.
sentences.zh: 基本上，《龙之家族》的情节就是坦格利安家族内部的内战。

sentences.en: And it ends up, so the end of series one, one of the rival candidates, who is a Targaryen herself and can ride a dragon,
sentences.zh: 故事最后，第一季结束时，其中一位竞争对手，她自己也是坦格利安人，也能骑龙，

sentences.en: is wondering whether she should fight to defend her right to the throne.
sentences.zh: 正在考虑是否应该为捍卫自己的王位继承权而战。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because she knows what it will mean.
sentences.zh: 因为她知道这意味着什么。

sentences.en: And there are these very, very kind of chilling lines that you get in the final episode of series one.
sentences.zh: 在第一季的最后一集中，有一些非常非常令人不寒而栗的台词。

sentences.en: When dragons flew to war before, so she's talking about what had happened even before this, everything burned.
sentences.zh: 当龙以前飞向战争时——所以她在谈论甚至在此之前发生的事情——一切都被烧毁了。

sentences.en: I do not wish to rule over a kingdom of ash and bone.
sentences.zh: 我不希望统治一个灰烬与白骨的王国。

sentences.en: And you see in the final stages of season one, you see how dragons actually can't be controlled, even by the people who supposedly can ride them.
sentences.zh: 在第一季的最后阶段，你会看到龙实际上是无法被控制的，即使是被那些理应能骑它们的人。

sentences.en: And I'm guessing that people listening to this, there will either be massive enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 我猜听这个节目的人，要么会充满热情。

sentences.en: I mean, Game of Thrones was a huge global phenomenon, and House of Dragons had a massive critical success as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，《权力的游戏》是一个巨大的全球现象，《龙之家族》也取得了巨大的评论成功。

sentences.en: But there will also be kind of bewilderment.
sentences.zh: 但也会有一种困惑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because there are lots of people, Tom, who would say, listening to this, say, oh, in a history podcast, dragons, really?
sentences.zh: 因为汤姆，有很多听众会说，哦，在历史播客里谈论龙，真的吗？

sentences.en: And actually, that itself is a historical phenomenon, because Tolkien, in 1936, correct and sober taste may refuse to admit that there can be an interest for us,
sentences.zh: 实际上，这本身就是一个历史现象，因为托尔金在 1936 年曾说，正确且清醒的品味可能会拒绝承认我们——

sentences.en: the proud we that includes all intelligent living people, in ogres and dragons.
sentences.zh: 那个包含所有聪明活人的“我们”——会对食人魔和龙感兴趣。

sentences.en: And actually, Tolkien, when he wrote that essay in the 30s, was saying, as a society, we have become indifferent to, we've lost sight of the, dare I say, the weirdness, Tom,
sentences.zh: 实际上，托尔金在 30 年代写那篇论文时是在说，作为一个社会，我们已经变得漠不关心，我们已经失去了对——我敢说——怪异事物的感知，汤姆，

sentences.en: of monsters, of dragons, and that we think of them as childish.
sentences.zh: 对怪物、对龙的感知，我们认为它们很幼稚。

sentences.en: But actually, they are a really, really interesting and important cultural and historical phenomenon that opens up all kinds of different avenues of inquiry.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，它们是一个非常非常有趣且重要的文化和历史现象，开启了各种不同的探究途径。

sentences.en: Well, the amazing thing is, is that even George R.
sentences.zh: 嗯，令人惊奇的是，即使是乔治·R.

sentences.en: R.
sentences.zh: R.

sentences.en: Martin, the novelist who created Game of Thrones, even he had to be persuaded to include dragons.
sentences.zh: 马丁，创造了《权力的游戏》的小说家，连他自己都不得不被说服去加入龙的元素。

sentences.en: So it was his friend, the writer, Phyllis Eisenstein, wrote to him and said,
sentences.zh: 所以是他的朋友，作家菲利斯·艾森斯坦写信给他，说，

sentences.en: George, it's a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 乔治，这是奇幻小说。

sentences.en: You've got to have dragons.
sentences.zh: 你必须得有龙。

sentences.en: George R.
sentences.zh: 乔治·R.

sentences.en: R.
sentences.zh: R.

sentences.en: Martin was doing the Wars of the Roses, basically,
sentences.zh: 马丁当时基本上是在写“玫瑰战争”，

sentences.en: Lannisters and Starks, Lancaster and York.
sentences.zh: 兰尼斯特和史塔克，兰开斯特和约克。

sentences.en: And I suppose he had an anxiety that putting dragons in it would mean that people thought it was childish, that it was silly and frivolous.
sentences.zh: 我想他担心加入龙会让人们觉得这很幼稚，觉得这很愚蠢和轻浮。

sentences.en: But as we'll discover, there's nothing frivolous about dragons at all, is there?
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将要发现的，龙一点也不轻浮，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think also, from the historical point of view, so looking at the dragon as a cultural phenomenon, there is a really obvious, strange factor about it,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为从历史的角度来看，把龙看作一种文化现象，它有一个非常明显、奇怪的因素，

sentences.en: which obviously, dragons are fantasy.
sentences.zh: 显然，龙是奇幻的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no disputing that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一点毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: Although, I think secretly, Tolkien kind of did believe that they might have existed.
sentences.zh: 尽管我认为托尔金私下里确实相信它们可能存在过。

sentences.en: He kind of drops hints about that in that essay that you were quoting.
sentences.zh: 他在你引用的那篇论文中暗示了这一点。

sentences.en: But the weird thing is that, basically, everyone kind of knows what they look like, even though they never existed.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，基本上每个人都知道它们长什么样，尽管它们从未存在过。

sentences.en: So you know that they're reptilian, that they kind of have scales, that they have lidless eyes, that they have a flickering tongue.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道它们是爬行动物，它们有鳞片，有无眼睑的眼睛，有分叉的舌头。

sentences.en: You know that they're long and snake-like, or you might say worm-like.
sentences.zh: 你知道它们又长又像蛇，或者你可以说像“长虫”。

sentences.en: So Tolkien, in that passage, that he quoted the worm.
sentences.zh: 所以托尔金在那段话里引用了“长虫”。

sentences.en: That they breathe fire, that they have wings, that they can fly, that they have legs.
sentences.zh: 它们会喷火，有翅膀，能飞，有腿。

sentences.en: Okay, just on legs.
sentences.zh: 好的，就说腿吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Two or four, Tom, because that is, among dragonologists, that is a crucial area of contention, isn't it, whether a dragon has two or four legs?
sentences.zh: 两条还是四条，汤姆？因为在龙类学家中，这是一个至关重要的争论领域，不是吗？龙是有两条腿还是四条腿？

sentences.en: Actually, specifically among British heralds, which we'll come to.
sentences.zh: 实际上，特别是在英国纹章官中，我们稍后会谈到。

sentences.en: So for British heraldry, a two-legged dragon is a wyvern, and a four-legged dragon is a dragon.
sentences.zh: 所以对于英国纹章学来说，两条腿的龙是双足飞龙，四条腿的才是龙。

sentences.en: We'll be coming to that.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: And Martin's dragons, so the dragons that you see in the House of the Dragon, are kind of midway between that.
sentences.zh: 马丁的龙，也就是你在《龙之家族》中看到的龙，介于两者之间。

sentences.en: So we'll be discussing that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会讨论这个。

sentences.en: Not quite three-legged, but...
sentences.zh: 不是三条腿，但是……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So everyone kind of, you know, if you said, what's a dragon?
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都……你知道，如果你问，什么是龙？

sentences.en: To someone in the West, they'd immediately know it.
sentences.zh: 对西方人来说，他们会立刻知道。

sentences.en: But the even weirder thing is, is that dragons are not confined to kind of medieval Europe.
sentences.zh: 但更奇怪的是，龙并不局限于中世纪的欧洲。

sentences.en: When people think of dragons, they think of China, don't they?
sentences.zh: 当人们想到龙时，他们会想到中国，不是吗？

sentences.en: But there are dragons also in...
sentences.zh: 但龙也存在于……

sentences.en: There are effectively dragons in Greek myths and Babylonian legends and so on.
sentences.zh: 希腊神话和巴比伦传说中实际上也有龙，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Egyptian.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有埃及。

sentences.en: So you could say it's kind of, pretty much a global phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说这几乎是一个全球性的现象。

sentences.en: So that raises the obvious question.
sentences.zh: 这就提出了一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: Where is this idea coming from?
